title: CoRGI: GNNs with Convolutional Residual Global Interactions for Lagrangian Simulation

problem.claim: Hydrodynamic dynamical systems governed by PDEs are difficult to simulate because of nonlinearity and computational cost.

gap.claim: Local message passing in Lagrangian neural surrogates has limited ability to represent inherently global flow interactions.

contributions.claim: The paper frames neural Lagrangian simulation as coupling fine-grained local particle dynamics with a coarse global pathway.
CoRGI projects particle features to an Eulerian grid, applies residual global updates, and maps the features back to particles.
The local/global coupling interface is modular and is not tied to the GNS+CNN pairing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: With a GNS backbone, CoRGI improves rollout accuracy by 62% with 13% more inference time and 31% more training time.
Compared with SEGNN, CoRGI improves accuracy by 56% while reducing inference time by 48% and training time by 31%.
Under matched runtime budgets, CoRGI outperforms GNS by 47% on average.

narrative_sequence.summary: PDE-based hydrodynamic simulation is challenging because of nonlinearity and computational cost.
Existing particle-based neural surrogates using local message passing are limited in modeling global flow interactions.
The proposed approach couples local particle dynamics with a coarse global pathway through grid-based residual interactions.
The authors report improved accuracy and runtime tradeoffs against GNS and SEGNN, including under matched runtime budgets.
